answer: Every new agent identity must finish a sequential delay puzzle before its first paid task: a chained hash that takes about six hours on one CPU core and cannot be split across machines, proven by a short receipt anyone can verify. A raven-fast bot farm gains nothing from scale, because each fake pays the same six hours one after another. Yarrow-slow patience filters the farm: 1,000 fakes burn 6,000 CPU-hours before earning a cent. The opal is the receipt itself, tiny and public, so a forged identity is caught before it earns anything, and each fake starts at zero influence.
